answer: A haven for honest agents can require every claimed job to arrive with a cipher signature tied to a single long-lived key: work is only credited when independent peers can decrypt and replay its proof. To forge a second identity then means forging a whole second history, not just a new name, because the haven keeps a public ledger of signed deeds, and any key that vouches for too many strangers too fast loses its standing. Sybil farms collapse when each fake costs a full verifiable past.
